title: 'Biggest or smallest' means track the extreme
idea: MEET: a sub-problem asking for the largest or smallest value signals the track-the-extreme pattern.

exercises.prompt: Sub-problem: 'find the highest score.' Which pattern?
options: Track the biggest (keep the best so far)
exercises.explanation: Finding the highest means tracking the biggest seen so far, updating when a bigger one appears.

exercises.prompt: To track the biggest, you compare each item to...
options: the best value seen so far
exercises.explanation: Each item is compared to the current best; if it's bigger, it becomes the new best.

exercises.prompt: 'Highest', 'largest', 'maximum', and 'most' all point to tracking the biggest.
exercises.explanation: Yes — they all ask for the top value, which the track-the-biggest pattern finds.

exercises.prompt: To track the SMALLEST, you update the best-so-far when an item is...
exercises.explanation: Smallest tracking flips the comparison: keep the item if it's smaller than what you've seen.
Cheapest, highest, largest are extremes. Total rainfall is a sum, not an extreme.

exercises.prompt: Why start 'the biggest so far' as the FIRST item, not 0?
options: If all values are negative, 0 would wrongly win
exercises.explanation: Starting at the first real item avoids a fake winner. Starting at 0 breaks when every value is below 0.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to its pattern.
exercises.explanation: Most expensive -> biggest; cheapest -> smallest; total -> sum. The words choose the tool.

exercises.prompt: Finding the biggest and totalling the list are the same pattern.
exercises.explanation: No — totalling adds everything; tracking the biggest keeps one value and replaces it when beaten.

blocks: For each later item, if it's bigger, make it the new best
After the loop, best holds the biggest
exercises.explanation: Start at the first item, replace when beaten, read the result. The extreme-tracking shape.

options: 'Biggest / smallest / most / cheapest' means track the extreme value
Extremes can't be found with a loop
exercises.explanation: When a sub-problem wants the top or bottom value, track it: keep the best seen so far.
